bib.title: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context

read.skipped: Nothing skipped. The 16-page ECCV version has no appendix; the category list, UIs and super-categories are in the extended arXiv version (CoRR abs/1405.0312), not read.

question: What dataset will best advance object recognition toward scene understanding, covering non-iconic views, contextual reasoning and precise 2D localisation?
hypothesis: Non-iconic images with many labelled, segmented instances per image will make a harder dataset, and models trained on it should generalise better to everyday scenes than models trained on prior datasets.
contributions: A dataset of 91 common object categories, 2.5M labelled instances in 328k images, with per-instance segmentation masks
A crowdsourced pipeline (category labelling, instance spotting, instance segmentation) on Amazon Mechanical Turk
Statistical comparison with PASCAL VOC, ImageNet and SUN
Baseline bounding-box and segmentation results with a Deformable Parts Model

method.summary: Images were collected from Flickr by searching pairs of object categories (or scene/object pairs) to get non-iconic images, then annotated on AMT in three stages: hierarchical category labelling (5 workers), instance spotting (5 workers), instance segmentation (1 trained worker). Baselines are DPMv5 detectors trained on PASCAL VOC 2012 or on COCO and tested on both, plus a segmentation-from-detection baseline using averaged aspect-specific masks.
method.task: object detection and instance segmentation dataset construction and benchmarking

datasets.name: MS COCO (2014 state)
datasets.size: 328,000 images; 2,500,000 labelled instances; 91 categories (82 with >5,000 instances); about 60,000 worker hours
datasets.split: 164,000 train, 82,000 validation, 82,000 test; duplicates removed (gist descriptors, Douze et al.) and splits made by date and user; annotations released for train and val, not test
datasets.source: Flickr photos; at most 5 photos per photographer within a short time window; annotation on Amazon Mechanical Turk
datasets.preprocessing: Tight-fitting bounding boxes derived from segmentation masks for the detection experiment; crowds of tightly grouped instances marked as one segment labelled 'do not care'. Segmentation stage still ongoing at publication.

datasets.name: COCO subset for DPM experiment
datasets.split: DPMv5-C trained on 5000 positive and 10000 negative images; 20 PASCAL categories

datasets.name: PASCAL VOC 2012
datasets.size: 20 categories over 11,000 images; >27,000 instance boxes, almost 7,000 with segmentations (as described in Related Work)

models.name: DPMv5-P
models.architecture: Deformable Parts Model, release 5 (Girshick et al.)

models.name: DPMv5-C
models.architecture: same DPMv5 implementation, default parameter settings

training.objective: DPM training (default release-5 settings); not detailed

other.segmentation_masks: aspect-specific pixel masks learned by averaging aligned training instance masks, one per DPM mixture component

inference.samples: single run per model; no seeds or variance reported

parameters.annotation_workers_instance_spotting: 5 per image, at most 10 instances of a category per worker per image
parameters.annotation_workers_segmentation: 1 per image, after a per-category training task (about 1 in 3 workers passed)

metrics.name: AP (average precision), detection
metrics.definition: per-category AP as in PASCAL VOC; correct detection needs box IoU >= 0.5; not defined further in text

metrics.name: Dataset-bias performance drop
metrics.definition: difference in AP of a model between two datasets (Torralba and Efros)

metrics.name: Segmentation overlap
metrics.definition: IoU of predicted and ground-truth masks, computed only over correct detections (box IoU >= 0.5)

metrics.name: Annotator recall/precision
metrics.definition: category labelling against expert union or majority vote

baselines: dataset statistics vs PASCAL VOC, ImageNet detection val, SUN
eval.protocol: Table 1 evaluates both models on PASCAL VOC 2012 and on MS COCO over the 20 PASCAL categories; annotation quality checked against seven expert co-authors; no significance tests.

results.quote: This stage took 17,751 worker hours to complete.

limits: Segmentation of all instances was unfinished at publication; the counts are for collected annotations.
Baselines are only DPMv5 on 20 PASCAL categories; no deep models trained or evaluated, and the authors expect CNN approaches to improve performance substantially.
The DPM training set for COCO is a 55k-image subset with 5000 positive and 10000 negative images; training hyperparameters are default and unreported.
Only 'thing' categories, no 'stuff'; no occlusion, keypoint or caption labels.
Segmentation annotated by a single worker per image; only a periodic check of quality.
The 91-category list, UIs and super-category list are not in this version (extended arXiv version).
Claim that COCO-trained models generalise better rests on one model family and a single run.
Captions are named only as future work; later COCO Captions and the AP averaged over IoU thresholds are not here.

terms.definition: Typical iconic-object images have a single large object in a canonical perspective centered in the image; iconic-scene images are shot from canonical viewpoints and commonly lack people.
'Thing' categories include objects for which individual instances may be easily labeled; 'stuff' categories include materials and objects with no clear boundaries.
category labels that are commonly used by humans when describing objects (dog, chair, person)
